Date: Thu, 6 Aug 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected token surge on June invoice — export attached

Hi Mina,

We're reviewing our June invoice and see an unexpected 42,134 token delta that pushed us into an overage tier. The spike doesn't map to any traffic patterns on our side — it's concentrated around a handful of async "replay" jobs that our telemetry shows as completed, but your usage export lists repeated requests between 2026-06-18 03:14:xx and 2026-06-18 03:19:xx.

I've attached a CSV export (quanta_june_async_replay_export.csv) and a PDF draft invoice highlighting the line item. Can you:
- Confirm whether those requests were counted server-side as normal inference tokens or as retried/orphaned jobs (double counted)
- Share any sampling logs or a pointer we can use to reconcile (request IDs, proxy session ids)
- Let us know the provisional credit policy while you investigate — we need to close our books next week.

We're happy to hop on a short call if it helps.

Thanks,
Sara Rahman
Head of Platform Reliability
QuantaHealth

Hi Sara — thanks for the export and the clear notes. I'm opening an internal investigation and looping in Ben (billing engineering) and Kimberly (finance) to triage.

Initial steps from our side:
1) Ben will run a targeted sample against the request IDs you attached and check our edge logs for retries and dedupe hits.
2) Kimberly will provisionally flag the invoice for review (won't push collection yet) while we validate.
3) If we find orphaned or double-counted replay jobs we will propose a provisional credit before you close the books.

Can you confirm whether those replay jobs were triggered by an automated backfill or a manual replay from your side? That will help narrow the root cause. Also, what timezone should we use when matching timestamps (looks like UTC vs your local TZ in the CSV).

I'll coordinate an update by EOD tomorrow. If you prefer a call, I can include our engineering lead; otherwise we'll communicate findings here.

Best,

Mina / Kim / Sara — I pulled a quick sample based on the request ids in Quanta's CSV. Preliminary notes:

- We see repeated CONNECT/POST sequences where the same client request id is present but multiple server-side sessions were created for the same logical job; this looks like a client-side retry that coincided with a short window of proxy instability on 2026-06-18 03:14–03:19 UTC.
- Our ingestion pipeline has a dedup window for async replay dedupe, but under heavy concurrency some ephemeral jobs can slip through if the client resends with a new session id while the previous session is still initializing — the result is two billed token streams for what the client perceived as one job.
- I attached a pointer to two sample request ids (r-9f3a, r-9f3b) and included the server trace snippets below for quick reference.

Suggested next steps:
1) We will run a full dedupe pass against Quanta's CSV and identify orphaned secondaries.
2) Finance (Kimberly) — recommend a provisional credit for the duplicated tokens while the pass completes; we typically cover confirmed double-bills for incidents with client-visible retries.
3) On the engineering side we'll add a mitigator to expand the dedupe handshake for replay flows and publish a short postmortem.

Sara, can you confirm whether you want the provisional credit applied as an invoice credit (preferred) or a one-time refund? We'll expedite whichever you choose.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Billing Engineering Lead
Redwood Inference

We confirmed on our side that an automated backfill triggered a tight loop of replays when a controller timed out and retried (we've since patched to add exponential backoff). We'd like the provisional credit applied as an invoice credit against the June bill — that works best for our finance team.

Next steps for me:
- I'll share confirmation from our deploy (small PR id 472) showing the backfill was the cause.
- Please share the final delta and the credit amount once Ben/Kimberly complete the dedupe pass.
- We can take a 20-min sync tomorrow if helpful — Mina, can you propose two 20-min slots?
